done_state: tessera/api/ provides a CLI and a localhost-only HTTP API (thin wrappers over store/gitops) with an SSE live-update stream that sees writes from other processes, docs/ file read/write as the sole write path with real cross-process locking, and discrepancy computation for the diff-vs-claim view, demonstrated end to end with a deliberately-mismatched claim. comment (CLI) and POST /tickets/:tid/comments (HTTP) also accept an optional code_snippet field (C12-C13, TESS-82), passed straight through to store.add_comment().

criteria.statement: CLI subcommands exist for create/get/list/comment/transition/link/set-field/set-reference-docs/claim/promote/rollback/stage-sync, each a thin call into store/gitops with no duplicated business logic.
HTTP API exposes equivalent JSON endpoints for the same operations as C1's CLI commands, returning the same underlying data.
The HTTP server binds 127.0.0.1 only -- a connection attempt to the same port on a real non-loopback interface address is refused, never silently accepted.

The SSE endpoint delivers a ticket event created by a DIFFERENT OS process (not just in-process writes) within the poll interval, proving the rowid-poll design actually closes the cross-process blind spot ARCHITECTURE.md's review found.

docs/ file writes go through api only, using flock(LOCK_EX) held across the full read-modify-write (not just a threading.Lock), restricted to paths under the docs/ root -- a path escaping docs/ (e.g. '../../etc/passwd') is rejected.
A docs/ file write emits no store event (a stated design decision, not an oversight) -- verified by asserting the events table row count is unchanged by a docs write.

discrepancy(ticket_id) compares a claim's files_touched against gitops's real diff files for the claimed commit and returns the set difference in both directions; a deliberately-mismatched claim (omits a touched file) is demonstrated to produce a non-empty discrepancy.
A claim matching the real diff exactly produces an empty discrepancy (no false positives).

HTTP responses use distinct, correct status codes: 201 on ticket creation, 400 on a WorkflowError/HierarchyError/CycleError from store (with the real error message in the body), 404 for a ticket id that doesn't exist -- not everything defaulting to 200.

actor identity threads from the CLI (--actor flag, required) and from the HTTP API (required JSON field) into every store/gitops call that records one -- a request missing it is rejected, not defaulted to a generic value that would defeat the audit trail.

create-ticket accepts an optional idempotency_key end to end through the HTTP layer and a retried request with the same key returns the same ticket_id (thin pass-through of store's already-proven guarantee, not re-implemented here).
CLI 'comment' command accepts an optional --code-snippet flag, passed through to store.add_comment(), retrievable via 'tessera get'.
HTTP POST /tickets/:tid/comments accepts an optional code_snippet key in the request body and passes it through to store.add_comment(); omitting it is unchanged behavior.
criteria.verification: python3 -m unittest tessera.api.tests.test_http_api exits 0 (all existing tests pass, plus a new passthrough test).

failure_criteria.statement: The localhost-only bind is only true in a comment, not in the actual server construction call.
failure_criteria.detection: C3 connects from a real non-loopback address and asserts refusal, not just reads the bind-call source.

failure_criteria.statement: A latency/throughput claim about the SSE poll appears with no reproduction path.
failure_criteria.detection: grep the diff for numeric claims; each must name the command that produced it.

failure_criteria.statement: api re-implements workflow/hierarchy/cycle/idempotency logic instead of calling store, risking drift from store's already-tested behavior.
failure_criteria.detection: api's ticket-mutation code paths call store methods directly; no duplicated validation logic exists in tessera/api/.

failure_criteria.statement: A store/gitops exception is caught in the HTTP layer and turned into a 200 with an error buried in the body, or logged and swallowed.
failure_criteria.detection: C9 asserts a non-200 status code specifically for each error class, not just that SOME response was returned.

failure_criteria.statement: The docs/ path-restriction check can be bypassed with a symlink or a '..'-containing path that resolves outside docs/ after normalization.
failure_criteria.detection: C5's path-restriction test uses a real '../' traversal attempt, checked against the RESOLVED path, not the raw string.

out_of_scope: Authentication/authorization (no auth in scope per SCOPE.md).
Rate limiting, request size limits beyond basic sanity.
A general-purpose web framework -- stdlib http.server only.
constraints: Python 3.9+ stdlib only (http.server, socketserver, argparse, json, fcntl, threading) plus tessera.common/store/gitops.
Server binds 127.0.0.1 explicitly, never an empty host string.
No business-logic duplication -- every mutation routes through store or gitops.
